text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--The European Commission president Jacques Santer's spokesman says it would be a catastrophe for the bloc if Denmark voted against the Amsterdam Treaty reforms in its referendum next year.

--Denmark's Burma Committee protests once more against Danish companies investing in Burma, notably cement and engineering group FLS Industries, wholesaler and graphics firm East Asiatic and DLH timber. The protest against the Rangoon regime's human rights abuses is supported by Burma's exile government, which has just held a secret meeting in Denmark.

--Denmark's small banks are booming as rarely before, with more clients and improved profits and the prospect of posting satisfactory first-half 1997 results on a level with their good 1996 performance, according to the chairman of the Danish Local Banks Association. In contrast the major banks are gripped in a competition wars.
--The larger Copenhagen hotels posted more overnights in July than last year, when room occupancy rose by 12 percent, according to hotelier sources.
